# 2 Samuel Chapter 5 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 172v–173r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_005_page_001.jpg, 2SA_005_page_002.jpg
**DSS:** 4QSamᵃ (4Q51) fragments extant for portions of 2 Samuel 5 — online reference at deadseascrolls.org.il

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** All the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron and said, "We are your bone and your flesh. **2** Even before, when Saul was king over us, it was you who led Israel out and brought them in. And the LORD said to you, 'You shall shepherd my people Israel, and you shall be ruler over Israel.'"

**3** So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and King David made a covenant with them at Hebron before the LORD, and they anointed David king over Israel.

**4** David was thirty years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years. **5** At Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months, and at Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah.

**6** The king and his men marched to Jerusalem against the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land. They said to David, "You will not come in here — even the blind and the lame will turn you away" — meaning, "David cannot come in here."

**7** But David captured the stronghold of Zion — that is, the City of David.

**8** David said on that day, "Whoever strikes the Jebusites, let him reach the water shaft — and the lame and the blind, who are hated by David's soul..." Therefore they say, "The blind and the lame shall not come into the house."

**9** David dwelt in the stronghold and called it the City of David. And David built up the city all around, from the Millo inward.

**10** David grew greater and greater, for the LORD, the God of hosts, was with him.

**11** Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, along with cedar trees, carpenters, and stonemasons, and they built David a house.

**12** And David knew that the LORD had established him as king over Israel and had exalted his kingdom for the sake of his people Israel.

**13** David took more concubines and wives from Jerusalem after he came from Hebron, and more sons and daughters were born to him. **14** These are the names of those born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, **15** Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia, **16** Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet.

**17** When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over Israel, all the Philistines went up to seek David. David heard of it and went down to the stronghold.

**18** The Philistines came and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim. **19** David inquired of the LORD, "Shall I go up against the Philistines? Will you give them into my hand?" The LORD said to David, "Go up, for I will certainly give the Philistines into your hand."

**20** David came to Baal-perazim and struck them there. He said, "The LORD has broken through my enemies before me like a breaking flood." Therefore that place was called Baal-perazim.

**21** They abandoned their idols there, and David and his men carried them away.

**22** The Philistines came up yet again and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim. **23** When David inquired of the LORD, he said, "You shall not go up. Circle around behind them and come upon them opposite the balsam trees. **24** When you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, move quickly — for then the LORD has gone out before you to strike the camp of the Philistines."

**25** David did as the LORD commanded him, and struck the Philistines from Geba to Gezer.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

All three translators agree on the chapter's tripartite structure: David anointed over all Israel (vv.1-5), the capture of Jerusalem (vv.6-12), and the two Philistine battles (vv.17-25). The Jebusite taunt passage (vv.6-8) is acknowledged as textually difficult by all three. The theological emphasis on YHWH's agency — YHWH establishes (v.12), YHWH breaks through (v.20), YHWH goes before (v.24) — is consistently rendered.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.1 — "Behold us" vs. "Look" vs. direct statement
- **EMET:** "Behold-us, your-bone and-your-flesh [are]-we"
- **LOGOS:** "Behold, we are your bone and your flesh"
- **PNEUMA:** "Look — we are your own flesh and blood"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "We are your bone and your flesh." Removes the archaic "behold" while preserving the Hebrew word order *atsm-kha u-vsar-kha*. "Flesh and blood" (PNEUMA) reverses the Hebrew order.

### V.6 — Jebusite taunt rendering
- **EMET:** "unless you-remove the-blind and-the-lame"
- **LOGOS:** "even the blind and the lame will turn you away"
- **PNEUMA:** "Even the blind and the lame could keep you out!"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "even the blind and the lame will turn you away" — LOGOS captures the taunt's force while maintaining formal register.

### V.8 — tsinnor rendering
- **EMET:** "through-the-water-shaft [tsinnor]"
- **LOGOS:** "the water shaft"
- **PNEUMA:** "up through the water shaft"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "the water shaft" — the term is debated (shaft, gutter, scaling-hook); the most neutral rendering preserves the ambiguity.

### V.9 — "Millo" vs. "terraced structure"
- **EMET:** "the-Millo"
- **LOGOS:** "the Millo"
- **PNEUMA:** "the terraced structure"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "the Millo" — the Hebrew term is a proper noun (*ha-millo'*). PNEUMA's "terraced structure" is an archaeological interpretation, not a translation.

### V.11 — "house" vs. "palace"
- **EMET:** "a-house"
- **LOGOS:** "a house"
- **PNEUMA:** "a palace"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "a house" — the Hebrew *bayit* means house/dwelling. "Palace" (PNEUMA) interprets the scale; the text simply says house.

### V.17 — "to seek David" vs. "to hunt him down"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "to seek David"
- **PNEUMA:** "to hunt him down"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "to seek David" — *levaqesh* means "to seek." PNEUMA adds hostile intent already implied by context.

### V.19 — "certainly give" (infinitive absolute)
- **EMET:** "giving I-will-give [naton etteyn]"
- **LOGOS:** "I will certainly give"
- **PNEUMA:** "I will hand...over to you"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "I will certainly give" — LOGOS correctly renders the emphatic infinitive absolute.

### V.20 — "breaking flood" vs. "breaking through of waters" vs. "dam breaking"
- **EMET:** "breaking-through of-waters [perets mayim]"
- **LOGOS:** "a breaking flood"
- **PNEUMA:** "a dam breaking"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "a breaking flood" — captures the force of *perets mayim* without adding "dam" (not in the text).

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
